questions.passage_md: The collection of rare maps in the university library ______ drawn by explorers in the sixteenth century.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: The subject is “collection” (singular), not “maps.” A singular subject takes the singular verb “includes.”

distractor_notes.A: “Include” is plural; it agrees with “maps,” which is inside a prepositional phrase and isn’t the subject.

questions.passage_md: After months of planning, the city orchestra announced that ______ spring season would include three works by living composers.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: The pronoun refers to “the city orchestra,” a single organization, so it takes the singular possessive “its.”

distractor_notes.A: “Their” is plural, but “orchestra” is a single group here.
distractor_notes.C: “It’s” means “it is,” which makes no sense here (“it is spring season”).
distractor_notes.D: “There” is a place word, not a possessive.

questions.passage_md: Last summer, Luis ______ a small vegetable garden behind his apartment building and gave most of the tomatoes to his neighbors.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: “Last summer” places the action in the past, and “gave” is past tense. “Planted” matches.

distractor_notes.D: Present progressive clashes with the past time frame.

questions.passage_md: The two ______ nests were built high in the same oak tree, only a few branches apart.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: The nests belong to two birds, so the plural possessive is needed: “birds’.”

distractor_notes.B: “Bird’s” is singular possessive, but there are two birds.

questions.passage_md: Walking through the botanical garden at dawn, ______
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: the smell of jasmine surprised Priya.
Priya was surprised by the smell of jasmine.
surprise came to Priya from the smell of jasmine.
the jasmine’s smell was surprising to Priya.
questions.explanation_md: The opening phrase “Walking through the botanical garden” must describe whoever comes right after the comma. Priya is the one walking, so “Priya” must come first.

distractor_notes.A: This says the *smell* was walking through the garden, a dangling modifier.
distractor_notes.D: This says the *jasmine’s smell* was walking.

questions.passage_md: Neither the head chef nor the servers ______ aware that the delivery of fresh fish had been delayed until the first orders came in.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: With “neither…nor,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “servers” (plural). The sentence is in the past, so “were” is correct.

distractor_notes.A: “Was” is singular, but the nearer subject, “servers,” is plural.
distractor_notes.D: “Has been” is singular and doesn’t fit the past time frame (“had been delayed”).

questions.passage_md: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet ______ home to roughly a quarter of all known marine species.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: The pronoun refers to “coral reefs” (plural), so “they are” is correct.

distractor_notes.A: “It” is singular and doesn’t agree with “reefs.”
distractor_notes.C: “Its” is a possessive and leaves the clause without a verb.
distractor_notes.D: “Their” is a possessive and leaves the clause without a verb.

questions.passage_md: By the time the rescue team reached the stranded hikers, the storm ______ for nearly two days.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: “By the time the rescue team reached” sets a past moment, and the storm had been going on before and up to that moment. The past perfect progressive “had been raging” expresses that.

distractor_notes.A: Present tense doesn’t fit the past time frame.
distractor_notes.B: Present perfect links the action to the present, not to a past moment.
distractor_notes.D: Future tense doesn’t fit a past event.

questions.passage_md: The findings of the study, which tracked more than 3,000 adults over two decades and was funded by several universities, ______ that regular walking may reduce the risk of memory loss.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: The subject is “findings” (plural). The long “which…” clause describes “the study” and sits between the subject and its verb. A plural subject needs “suggest.”

distractor_notes.A: “Suggests” agrees with “study,” which is not the subject.

questions.passage_md: The committee praised the proposal for being affordable, easy to maintain, and ______
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: it would benefit the whole neighborhood.
benefiting the whole neighborhood would happen.
the whole neighborhood would benefit from it.
questions.explanation_md: Items in a list should share the same form. “Affordable” and “easy to maintain” are adjectives or adjective phrases, so the third item should be too: “beneficial to the whole neighborhood.”

distractor_notes.A: This is a full clause, which breaks the parallel list.
distractor_notes.C: This awkward clause breaks the parallel structure.
distractor_notes.D: This is a full clause, which breaks the parallel list.

questions.passage_md: Every one of the paintings in the exhibition, including the three that were loaned by private collectors, ______ insured against damage during shipping.
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation_md: The subject is “Every one” (singular). “Of the paintings” and the “including…” phrase don’t change the subject, so it takes the singular “was.”

distractor_notes.A: “Were” is plural; it agrees with “paintings” or “three,” neither of which is the subject.

questions.passage_md: Having analyzed decades of rainfall records from dozens of weather stations, ______
questions.stem_md: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: the conclusion reached by climatologist Ana Brito was that the region’s dry seasons are lengthening.
the region’s dry seasons, according to climatologist Ana Brito, are lengthening.
climatologist Ana Brito concluded that the region’s dry seasons are lengthening.
it was concluded by climatologist Ana Brito that the region’s dry seasons are lengthening.
questions.explanation_md: “Having analyzed decades of rainfall records” describes whoever did the analysis, so that person must come right after the comma: “climatologist Ana Brito concluded….”

distractor_notes.A: This says “the conclusion” analyzed the records.
distractor_notes.B: This says “the region’s dry seasons” analyzed the records.
distractor_notes.D: “It” comes right after the modifier, so there is no clear person doing the analyzing.
